overview: The naming here trips up a lot of people — 'RT' means reverse transcription, and it's easy to confuse with real-time.
genZNote: Detects the RNA, or detects it and tells you how much.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: Reverse Transcription PCR — converts an RNA target into complementary DNA (cDNA) via reverse transcriptase, then amplifies it by conventional end-point PCR.
aspects.valueB: Reverse Transcription quantitative PCR — the same reverse transcription step, but followed by real-time quantitative PCR rather than end-point detection.

aspects.label: Detection Method
aspects.valueA: End-point detection, typically via gel electrophoresis after amplification finishes.
aspects.valueB: Real-time fluorescence detection during amplification, exactly as in standard qPCR.

aspects.label: Quantification
aspects.valueA: Qualitative presence/absence, or at best rough semi-quantitative estimation.
aspects.valueB: True quantification of starting RNA amount via Ct value and a standard curve.

aspects.label: Common Terminology Confusion
aspects.valueA: 'RT-PCR' is often loosely (and incorrectly) used in casual speech to mean 'real-time PCR.'
aspects.valueB: The correct term for what most people actually mean when they say 'real-time RT-PCR' for RNA virus testing (e.g. SARS-CoV-2).

aspects.label: Typical Application
aspects.valueA: Basic detection of an RNA target's presence, cloning of cDNA for downstream work.
aspects.valueB: Clinical RNA virus diagnostics and viral load monitoring, where both detection and quantification matter.

aspects.label: Workflow Steps
aspects.valueA: Reverse transcription, then a separate conventional PCR, then gel visualization.
aspects.valueB: Reverse transcription followed immediately by real-time PCR in the same or a coupled reaction, with continuous fluorescence monitoring.

overlay.commonMisconception: "RT" stands for reverse transcription, not real-time — the confusion between RT-PCR and real-time PCR is one of the most common mix-ups in molecular diagnostics.
